title: Continuity of the pair length
statement: Let $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous on $[0,1]$, and let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$. For any $m\ge 0$ and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, the function $t\mapsto L(t,0)$ is continuous on $[0,1]$.
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. If $P$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and $a+b,a-b\in[0,1]$, then $t\mapsto L(t,0)$ is continuous on $[0,1]$.
